insight.title: Why the tallest trees never touch
insight.subtitle: A lesson in grace from the forest canopy

sections.text: Look up and see the sky through a jigsaw. In many dense forests, tree species refuse to let their branches overlap. They grow toward each other but stop just inches away. This creates winding, sunlit paths through the leaves like rivers of light. It is a quiet, leafy dance of mutual respect.

This phenomenon, called crown shyness, ensures every branch receives sunlight. By maintaining this delicate gap, trees avoid rubbing together in the wind, protecting their sensitive buds from damage. It is a calculated social distance. They share the sky without competition, allowing life to flourish in the shadows they curate.

Your day is often a series of crowded intersections. We rush and collide, forgetting the elegance of the gap. Nature reminds us that the space between things is as vital as the things themselves. Boundaries are not walls. They are the breathing room that allows everyone to find their light.

ENDING RULE:
Sometimes, the best support is to leave exactly enough room to grow.

news.title: India's Resilience Shines Amid Global Challenges: Jaishankar at IIM Raipur
news.description: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar addressed the 15th convocation at IIM Raipur, highlighting India's resilience amid global shocks like the West Asia conflict. He emphasized India's growth into a top five economy, the importance of self-reliance, and the evolving role of foreign policy in promoting 'Brand India.'
news.why: A stable economy could protect your current job and salary growth.

news.title: India navigates global shocks successfully, says EAM Jaishankar at IIM Raipur
news.description: S Jaishankar hails Indias resilience to global shocks at IIM Raipur, outlines Viksit Bharat 2047 vision, digital progress and confident foreign policy
news.why: You may face fewer sudden price spikes for fuel and food.

news.title: Stalin Slams FCRA Amendment Bill as 'Draconian'
news.description: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M K Stalin criticized the Centre's proposed FCRA Amendment Bill 2026 as 'draconian', claiming it targets minorities. He urged its withdrawal and accused the BJP-led government of failing in foreign policy and in protecting Tamil Nadu fishermen. Stalin noted the bill infringes on constitutional rights and religious freedom.
news.why: Local charities you rely on could lose funding for essential services.

news.title: With Iran war and LPG crisis, it’s time to ask: How does India’s foreign policy impact its people?
news.description: A common argument often made in the past about foreign policy is that it is not an issue of the masses. It is decided by the elites and does not concern the everyday lives of the people. Times have changed, and the impact is regular and vivid
news.why: Your monthly cooking gas bills may increase due to foreign conflicts.

news.title: Iran War To Op Sindoor: Congress Leaders Who Didn't Toe Party Line, Backed Centre's Stance
news.description: Rahul Gandhi described India’s foreign policy under PM Modi as “compromised”. In contrast, Shashi Tharoor called it “responsible statecraft”.
news.why: Unified government policy could speed up your evacuation during foreign wars.

news.title: Apple CarPlay Just Got Three Popular iPhone Apps
news.description: Apple's CarPlay system for accessing iPhone apps on a vehicle's dashboard screen received three popular apps this week: ChatGPT, Google Meet, and Audiomack. CarPlay Ultra in an Aston Martin In addition, WhatsApp is beta testing a revamped CarPlay app that will improve upon the basic Siri-based functionality that was previously available. Make sure you have the latest version of each app and they will automatically appear on CarPlay.
news.why: Your car dashboard could offer new tools to simplify your commute.
